title: Garlic Bread (Italian Style)
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Italian-style garlic bread is a crusty loaf split and slathered with a fragrant blend of butter, olive oil, roasted garlic, and parsley, then baked until golden and irresistible.
longDesc: While garlic bread as a specific dish is more of an Italian-American creation, its roots lie firmly in the Italian tradition of bruschetta and fettunta — bread rubbed with garlic and drizzled with olive oil — dressed up here with butter and a hot oven for a richer, restaurant-style result.
ingredients: 1 loaf ciabatta or Pane Pugliese, split lengthwise
30 ml (2 tbsp) extra virgin olive oil
6 garlic cloves, finely minced or grated
steps: In a small bowl, mash together the softened butter, olive oil, garlic, parsley, half the Parmigiano, salt, and red pepper flakes if using, until well combined.
Spread the garlic butter generously and evenly over the cut sides of the bread.
Sprinkle the remaining Parmigiano over the top.
Place cut-side up on a baking sheet and bake for 10–12 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
For extra color, switch to the broiler for the final 1–2 minutes, watching closely so it doesn't burn.
Slice and serve immediately while hot.
chefTips: Grating the garlic rather than mincing it gives a more even, milder flavor throughout the butter.
Let the butter come fully to room temperature for easy, even spreading.
Broiling briefly at the end gives the best golden, slightly crisp top.
commonMistakes: Using cold, hard butter, which tears the bread when spreading.
Burning the garlic under the broiler — watch it closely in the final minute.
Using pre-minced jarred garlic, which lacks the fresh, sharp aroma of freshly minced cloves.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Unbaked garlic butter can be refrigerated for up to a week or frozen for a month.
reheating: Reheat in a 180°C (350°F) oven for 5 minutes to re-crisp.
healthBenefits: Garlic contains allicin, associated with immune and cardiovascular benefits.
Parsley adds vitamin K and vitamin C.
culturalNote: While not a traditional dish found on menus within Italy itself, Italian-style garlic bread has become one of the most beloved Italian-inspired dishes worldwide, especially as a pasta-night side.
